mechanism: Paul Hudson's resignation as a director of Sanofi and the associated financial arrangements.
raw_text: Paul Hudson resigned from his position as director, with immediate effect. In accordance with the recommendations of the AFEP-MEDEF Code, Sanofi hereby publishes the information regarding the financial arrangements for the departure of Paul Hudson, whose office as Chief Executive Officer of Sanofi terminated on February 17, 2026 end-of-day pursuant to the decision taken by the Board of Directors on February 11, 2026.

mechanism: Paul Hudson's pro-rata fixed compensation for 2026 up to the date of his resignation.
raw_text: Paul Hudson will receive, on a pro rata basis through February 17, 2026 inclusive (the date of termination of his office as Chief Executive Officer), the fixed portion of his annual compensation.

mechanism: Paul Hudson's annual variable compensation for 2025, subject to shareholder approval.
raw_text: the Board set Paul Hudson's annual variable compensation for 2025 at a gross amount of €2,616,000, representing 163.53% of his fixed compensation. In accordance with Article L. 22-10-34 II of the French Commercial Code, payment of Paul Hudson's variable compensation for 2025 will be subject to prior approval by the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders held to vote on the financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, and scheduled for April 29, 2026.

raw_text:
Sanofi ranking within the panel TSR Allocation Rate
1st or 2nd 125%

mechanism: The attainment level for the TSR criterion determines the delivery of performance shares.
raw_text: The attainment level for the TSR criterion (80% of the award) will be determined at the end of the five-year vesting period, which runs from April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2031.

mechanism: The Business EPS criterion affects the award of shares.
raw_text: The Business EPS criterion accounts for 30% of the award (Business EPS represents Sanofi's “business net income” divided by the number of Sanofi shares), and is determined as the average actual-to-budget ratio of Business EPS attained over the entire vesting period at constant exchange rates.

mechanism: The adoption of a clawback policy by the Board of Directors on October 26, 2023, requires Sanofi to recover erroneously-awarded compensation from the Chief Executive Officer and other key executives.
raw_text: On October 26, 2023, the Board of Directors adopted a clawback policy under which Sanofi must, within a reasonable time-frame, recover the portion of the Chief Executive Officer’s variable compensation (cash-based or equity-based) that is wholly or partly contingent on the attainment of financial performance criteria and was paid to her (according to the definition contained in the NASDAQ listing rules) based on financial information that has been determined to be erroneous and has required accounting restatement to correct an error in previously-published financial statements.

mechanism: Paul Hudson's variable compensation for 2025 was incorrectly reported as 100% achievement rate instead of the correct 109%.
raw_text: In Item 6 of the Form 20-F for 2025, an error appeared in the table on pages 129 and 130 presenting the achievement level of the performance conditions related to Paul Hudson’s 2025 variable remuneration. In the column ‘2025 Achievement Rate’, the correct figure is ‘109%’ and not ‘100%’

mechanism: Paul Hudson will receive the variable portion of his annual compensation on a pro rata basis through February 17, 2026.
raw_text: Paul Hudson will receive, on a pro rata basis through February 17, 2026 inclusive (the date of termination of his office as Chief Executive Officer), the variable portion of his annual compensation.

mechanism: Paul Hudson will not be awarded any performance shares in respect of 2026 due to the termination of his office as Chief Executive Officer.
raw_text: Given the decision by the Board of Directors to terminate Paul Hudson’s office as Chief Executive Officer effective February 17, 2026, it was resolved not to award him any performance shares in respect of 2026.

mechanism: Paul Hudson will retain the benefit of performance shares awarded to him on April 30, 2024 and April 30, 2025 on a pro rata basis.
raw_text: Paul Hudson will retain the benefit of the performance shares awarded to him on April 30, 2024, and April 30, 2025 under the 2024 and 2025 annual plans, on a pro rata basis over the respective vesting periods of those plans.

mechanism: Paul Hudson will cease to be a member of Sanofi’s top-up defined-contribution pension plan and will no longer benefit from the related annual contribution.
raw_text: Paul Hudson will cease to be a member of Sanofi’s top-up defined-contribution pension plan and will no longer benefit from the related annual contribution.

mechanism: Paul Hudson is entitled to the top-up defined-contribution pension plan for 2025, with an annual contribution of up to 25% of his reference compensation.
raw_text: Paul Hudson is entitled to the top-up defined-contribution pension plan introduced within Sanofi on January 1, 2020. Under the terms of that plan, the Chief Executive Officer receives an annual contribution the amount of which (subject to attainment of a performance condition) may be up to 25% of his reference compensation (annual fixed and variable compensation).

mechanism: Paul Hudson will receive a gross termination benefit of €5,207,750.
raw_text: Paul Hudson will therefore receive a gross termination benefit of €5,207,750, corresponding to the termination benefit cap less the amount of the non-compete indemnity (see below).

mechanism: Paul Hudson will receive an indemnity of €3,124,650 for a non-compete undertaking.
raw_text: In return for that undertaking, and subject to compliance therewith, Paul Hudson will receive an indemnity of €3,124,650, corresponding to 9 months of total compensation (based on his fixed compensation in effect on the date of termination and the last variable compensation received prior to that date, i.e. the variable compensation for 2024 that he received in 2025), paid in 9 installments.

mechanism: The Board of Directors set the compensation package for the future Chief Executive Officer, Belén Garijo, on March 4, 2026, aiming to align her compensation with long-term value creation and shareholder interests.
raw_text: The compensation package and amounts awarded to the future Chief Executive Officer were set by the Board of Directors on March 4, 2026, acting on a recommendation from the Compensation Committee and taking account of Belén Garijo’s profile.

mechanism: The Board of Directors decided to adopt a stable, transparent approach for equity-based compensation, splitting it into long-term and medium-term tranches to incentivize long-term performance.
raw_text: For equity-based compensation, and in line with the aforementioned value-creation objective, the Board of Directors decided, acting on a recommendation from the Compensation Committee, to adopt a stable, transparent approach that splits the equity-based compensation for the Chief Executive Officer’s future term of office into two equal components, as described below:

mechanism: The Board of Directors awarded Belén Garijo an international relocation benefit to account for her relocation needs, which is expected to impact her compensation over a four-year period.
raw_text: Acting on a proposal from the Compensation Committee, the Board of Directors also decided to award Belén Garijo an international relocation benefit, capped at 15% of her target annual compensation (fixed plus variable), over a four-year period, to take account of the relocation needed for her to take up her role; her current place of residence; her nationality; her profile, having already served in a CEO role; and the exceptional, time-limited strategic priorities she has been set by the Board of Directors (see above).

mechanism: The maximum termination benefit for Belén Garijo in the event of forced departure from Sanofi was reduced from 24 months to 12 months of latest total compensation.
raw_text: In addition, the maximum termination benefit she can receive in the event of forced departure from Sanofi is reduced from 24 months of latest total compensation to 12 months.

mechanism: The future Chief Executive Officer will not be entitled to the Sanofi top-up defined-contribution pension scheme, which could have represented a benefit of up to 25% of her reference compensation.
raw_text: Finally, unlike Paul Hudson, the future Chief Executive Officer will not be entitled to the Sanofi top-up defined-contribution pension scheme, which could have represented a benefit of up to 25% of her reference compensation (fixed + annual variable).

The Trump administration's drug pricing policies, particularly the MFN rule and the TrumpRx.gov initiative, represent a significant paradigm shift.

The administration's threat of a Section 301 investigation into trade partners' drug pricing practices further signals a global re-calibration of pharmaceutical commerce, potentially leading to higher drug prices in other countries as the U.S. seeks to lower its own.
The current administration's approach, blending direct negotiation with market-based solutions like TrumpRx.gov and tariff exemptions, presents a nuanced challenge.

The 'Big Beautiful Bill' signed in August 2025, which allows drugmakers to exempt more products from Medicare price negotiations, might seem to favor the industry, but the overall direction is towards greater price control.
Sanofi is poised for continued growth driven by Dupixent, especially with its expanding approvals in significant markets like Europe and Canada for conditions such as COPD.
The completion of its €5 billion share buyback program in 2025 is expected to provide continued support for its stock price.

Sanofi may need to consider strategic pivots, such as increasing its focus on global markets less affected by aggressive U.S. pricing policies or investing more heavily in biosimilar development to diversify its portfolio.
Sustained pressure on drug prices, potentially impacting profit margins and forcing a re-evaluation of R&D investment priorities.
More drugmakers voluntarily entering into MFN-like agreements to avoid tariffs and gain access to direct-to-consumer platforms like TrumpRx.gov, leading to a gradual reduction in U.S. drug prices.

Increased litigation and pushback from the industry, challenging the legality and implementation of aggressive pricing policies, potentially leading to a more drawn-out and contentious reform process.

The success of TrumpRx.gov in driving down consumer costs and increasing access will also be a critical factor in determining the long-term viability and expansion of such government-backed platforms.
